correctness.rationale: The complete gradient Gram spectrum and both extremal switches check analytically. Frobenius unit trace-free symmetric matrices have global Dirichlet norm squared 4/(d+2). In the normalized Z,C,S sector the longitude-zero diagonal is (1,1−2/d,1+2/d), with only Z–C off diagonal, sqrt((d−2)/d); rotation then gives the longitude harmonics of orders 2 and 4. The mixed pair has zero-longitude values 1±(d−2)/(2d), and transverse trace-free quadratics contribute the mass eigenvalue. Integration gives the stated blocks and multiplicities. With t=cos L, the competing odd planar branch meets an extremal radial branch only at t²=d(d−2)/8; for d=4 the solutions are excluded endpoints, and only d=3 gives interior ties. The radial determinant divided by the mass squared is (d+2)L²/(3d)+O(L⁴), giving the reported condition-number constants. Analyticity proves strict positivity on both the lune and its complement. The independent cubature reproduced 24 full Gram spectra including both switch apertures; the all-parameter proof does not depend on sampling. Square radius has the beta law as in RESULT.md; the radial notation in one verifier comment does not affect its moments.
residual_risks: Only pure degree two and full tangential gradients; no regional Laplace boundary problem or bound for mixed-degree spaces.

The dimension-three-only pair of switches and the sharp narrow-lune conditioning law distinguish genuinely different observation behavior from scalar concentration and from caps.
